extracted.intended_audience: patent researchers, patent economists, USPTO analysts, patent analytics vendors, and policy analysts evaluating patent quality metrics
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing patent quality using forward-citation information, with methods to distinguish technologically-informative citations from formal/strategic citations using NLP similarity and cohort comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raw forward citation count
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute raw forward citation count (total number of later patents that cite the focal patent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as a useful screening signal but not as the primary high-stakes quality measure: 'The naive citation count remains useful as a screening signal but should not be the primary quality measure for high-stakes assessments.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Technologically-similar citation count
rubrics_metrics.description: Count only forward citations where the citing and cited patents have above-threshold technological similarity (i.e., substantive/technological citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify substantive citations via an NLP-derived similarity threshold; these 'similar' citations are more predictive of quality than raw citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Similarity-weighted citation score
rubrics_metrics.description: Weight each forward citation by its measured technological similarity to the focal patent, producing a similarity-weighted citation score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives more weight to substantive citations and less to formal/strategic references; authors find this substantially improves predictive power versus raw counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratio of similar-to-total citations (citation informativeness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the ratio of technologically-similar citations to total forward citations to indicate how informative the citation stream is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A high similar/total ratio indicates informative citation patterns; a low ratio suggests many citations are formal or strategic and that raw counts overstate quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohort comparison of similarity-weighted/similar citation counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare a patent's similar-citation count or similarity-weighted score to the distribution for its cohort (time/technology cohort).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cohort percentiles for interpretation; 'Top quartile of similar citations = high quality.' Cohort adjustment helps correct for temporal and field differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation source diversity (across art units)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether forward citations come from a diversity of art units or classifications, indicating cross-field impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations from diverse art units signal higher originality and broader technological impact; concentrations suggest limited cross-field relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations from major industry firms (commercial validation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag forward citations originating from major industry firms as indicators of commercial relevance and validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations by established industry actors increase confidence in commercial or practical significance of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation acceleration over time
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate citation growth patterns, specifically whether citations grow/accelerate in years 5-10 post-grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An accelerating citation pattern in years 5–10 post-grant is a strong marker of continued relevance and high quality; include time-series patterns in assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early stagnation of citations as a weak marker
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations that stagnate or decline after the first 3 years post-grant are indicative of weaker quality or limited continuing relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early drop-off implies the patent did not gain sustained technological or commercial traction; treat such patents cautiously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward citations from technologically dissimilar patents (formal/strategic citations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Forward citations where citing and cited patents are technologically dissimilar are often formal or strategic (defensive, blocking) and less informative about substantive quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat such dissimilar citations as weak quality markers; consider down-weighting or excluding them from quality measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations concentrated in a single art unit
rubrics_metrics.description: When forward citations are concentrated within one art unit or narrow classification, the patent shows limited cross-field impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentration is a weak quality signal compared with cross-art-unit citation diversity; it suggests narrow influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations only from minor entities or own firm (self/insular citations)
rubrics_metrics.description: If forward citations come predominantly from minor entities or the patent owner's own firm, they may reflect low external validation or strategic/self-citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such citation sources weaken the evidentiary value of citation counts for quality assessment; flag and discount these patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations appearing in litigation context (litigation citations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of citations in litigation or enforcement contexts indicates commercial significance and can be a quality marker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Litigation-linked citations are a strong signal of commercial value; include litigation/contextual flags in quality scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic citation portfolio/owner markers
rubrics_metrics.description: Ownership or portfolio characteristics—membership in cross-licensing portfolios, standard-essential portfolios, or ownership by a prolific patentee—are markers that many citations may be strategic rather than informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When these markers are present, treat forward citations with caution and consider applying higher similarity thresholds or additional discounting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informative Citation Subsetting (operational rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational procedure: subset the citation set to only those citations that meet technological-similarity thresholds before counting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 'informative citation subsetting' reduces noise from formal/strategic citations and yields more predictive citation-based quality measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vector-space patent-text similarity (NLP validation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use vector-space/NLP patent-text similarity models to estimate technological similarity between patents and validate whether a citation is technologically informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors develop and endorse vector-space similarity methods as the means to implement similarity-weighting and subsetting; commercial analytics and USPTO research are adopting these approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust for citation concentration and distributional skew
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that a small minority of patent applications generate the majority of patent citations (high skew/concentration), which affects interpretation of counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of skewed distributions, rely on weighted/subsetted measures and cohort percentiles rather than raw counts alone to avoid overemphasizing outliers or strategic citation clusters.
